Incompetent

A terrible experience. I brought my two-month-old kitten, who was severely malnourished because he was a stray, to the clinic. He had very severe giardia. The doctor prescribed antibiotics, but despite this, he was given a booster vaccine right away.
The next day, the kitten had a change of heart, and when I took him to another vet, it turned out that the vaccine was the cause, and that it shouldn't have been administered so hastily to an already debilitated kitten. Instead, it was necessary to wait for the giardia to clear up first. Furthermore, a subsequent test revealed FIV, which further aggravated the already very delicate situation, leading to his death.
Now I wonder why the doctor thought of vaccinating a two-month-old kitten weighing 700 grams, malnourished, who was already fighting the giardia parasite and was on antibiotics, when ALL the other vets I spoke to gave me the same answer: "The vaccine should have been administered after a few days on a kitten like this." "debilitated"
It was a real mistake, both on our part in putting our kitten in the wrong hands, and a great deal of negligence on your part.
I acknowledge your response, which clearly decontextualizes and manipulates the facts in an attempt to defend a serious medical error. All international protocols (WSAVA) prohibit vaccinating a debilitated animal with active Giardia and on antibiotics. The vaccine overloaded an already compromised immune system, causing it to collapse. FIV aggravated the situation, but the trigger was your hasty decision. Saying that tests are only done after 6 months IS A PRETEXT: on a seriously ill cat, they are performed immediately to obtain a complete picture.
I also strongly reject the slander about attempted "bribery." Having never handled a seized dog, we simply asked her about the available options and whether there were places or organizations willing to sterilize her, for the sole humanitarian purpose of preventing mammary tumors and possibly causing her avoidable suffering. NO MONEY WAS NEVER OFFERED. Using a request for guidance to divert attention from the kitten's death is incorrect and ethically reprehensible.
